newsitem.title: ITALY: GTE to concentrate on bid for Italy's SEAT.
newsitem.headline: GTE to concentrate on bid for Italy's SEAT.

text.p: U.S. telecom group GTE Corp confirmed it was pulling out of a consortium to compete for Italy's third mobile phone licence, saying it would concentrate on competing for Italian phone directory publisher SEAT.
GTE has been shortlisted as a potential buyer in the sell-off of state owned SEAT, which was split off from state telecoms holding Stet at the start of this year.

"This decision (to leave the consortium) allows GTE to concentrate much more on the SEAT operation, in which it continues to show strong interest, and will allow GTE to examine other opportunities which might present themselves in Europe," a statement from the group said.
The sale of SEAT is due to be carried out by mid-June and state industrial holding IRI has said it has received eight non-binding offers for the company.

GTE had been part of a consortium which includes Italian broadcaster Mediaset preparing to bid for Italy's PCN standard mobile phone licence when it was offered. Mediaset said this week GTE had bowed out.

"GTE entered the consortium with the objective of evaluating the practicability of this initiative and has concluded that this opportunity, while still advantageous for the partners, no longer coincides with GTE's current strategy," it said.
Norway's Telenor, British Telecom and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) remain with Mediaset in the consortium.
